text:
marta: quick cross-check — for Private mode we need a final call on secret propagation. Do we want control plane to push ephemeral creds into the runtime, or should runtimes pull from customer KMS and we only exchange a reference?

tom_k: +1 we should minimize control plane holding plaintext. but pushing can simplify onboarding and reduce runtime complexity. tradeoffs: attack surface vs operational friction.

alex_r: my vote is for references + runtime pull. That keeps Private truly private (control plane never sees keys). but it means we need robust auth delegation and a simple probe flow so runtimes can validate they can access the KMS.

sree_p: agree with alex. Also think about failure modes: if runtime can't reach KMS at boot we need fallback to a short-lived pushed token for bootstrap. Maybe control plane can issue a one-time bootstrap token encrypted to the runtime's TPM/HSM.

julia: ops question — how do we debug auth failures without access to keys? Need good error codes and a decorrelated telemetry surface that tells us "kms-unreachable" vs "invalid-creds" without exposing secrets.

ops-bot: incident 1778885001 opened: observed 3 customer Private deployments with KMS timeouts last 24h. linking.

marta: good catch. Proposal: primary = reference + runtime pull. fallback = control plane-issued encrypted bootstrap token that expires in 5m. Runtime should emit structured error events: KMS_UNREACHABLE, TOKEN_EXPIRED, PERMISSION_DENIED.

alex_r: +1. Implementation notes: we need a capability discovery RPC on runtime so control plane can ask: "supports-kms-pull? supports-hsm-binding?" could be simple HTTP `/capabilities` returning a JSON blob. Example: 
```
GET /capabilities
200 {
  "kms_pull": true,
  "hsm_binding": true,
  "bootstrap_token_supported": true
}
```

sree_p: also suggest a lightweight probe endpoint `/probe-auth` that attempts to fetch from KMS and returns non-sensitive status codes, e.g. 200 OK, 502 KMS_UNREACHABLE, 403 KMS_FORBIDDEN. That lets us avoid pushing tokens preemptively.

julia: how will rollout look? We must support older runtimes that don't implement capabilities. fallback behavior for those should be documented — assume they require control-plane push but mark them deprecated.

marta: action items: 1) alex to draft small-ish RFC for reference-first + encrypted bootstrap fallback (due EOW). 2) sree to spec `/capabilities` and `/probe-auth` (POC two-endpoint contract). 3) eng-sre to add telemetry mapping (labels for KMS_UNREACHABLE/TOKEN_EXPIRED). 4) product to add migration notes for customers moving to Private.

alex_r: will include sample manifest snippet showing reference style:
```
secrets:
  model_key_ref: "kms://projects/acme/keys/model-serve-key"
  bootstrap_policy: "encrypted-bootstrap:true"
```

marta: tiny UX ask — console should surface a clear modal: "Runtime could not access KMS — provide a one-time bootstrap token?" only when runtime advertises `bootstrap_token_supported`.

julia: +1. Also require audit events for any control-plane-supplied bootstrap token issuance. HSM binding must be surfaced in audit logs.

tom_k: we should also document latency SLO impact: KMS pull adds 50-200ms on cold start depending on region. suggest local caching with TTL tied to key rotation. note in RFC.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: draft RFC branch pushed to repo /rfc/private-secret-propagation by alex_r.

marta: thanks all. I'll collect notes and convert into an RFC skeleton tonight. If anyone has strong objections to reference-first approach speak up now, otherwise we'll move forward with RFC + POC.

sree_p: no objections. small nit: make sure bootstrap token expiry is configurable per-customer.

marta: noted. closing thread for now — RFC comments in PR. :white_check_mark:
